plan: [ This is a sealed-bid second-price auction: the winner pays the highest competing bid. With independent private values and risk neutrality, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy that maximizes expected profit over time. There is no relevant history to exploit in this single round. By bidding exactly my value ($21), I win whenever the “price to win” is below 21 and pay that lower price, and I avoid overpaying if others value it more. Therefore, bid truthfully at 21.0. ]

[ This is a sealed-bid second-price auction: if I win, I pay the highest competing bid. With independent private values and risk neutrality, the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Underbidding risks losing when winning would be profitable; overbidding risks paying more than my value if others bid between my value and my bid. Tie-breaking randomization does not change this conclusion. Therefore, to maximize expected profit this round (and in the long run), I will bid exactly my value of 22. ]

[ This is a sealed-bid second-price auction: if I win, I pay the highest competing bid, not my own. In such auctions, bidding my true value weakly dominates all other strategies—overbidding risks paying above value; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With value = 13 and no informative history (1 round), optimal long-run and short-run policy is truthful bidding. Tie-breaking is random; bidding exactly 13 preserves optimality. ]
